source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide whether a shadow will form, and how dark it will be, from how the object blocks light before it reaches a screen.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The object still casts a distinct shadow on the wall when all lights are off.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: An object that blocks more light makes a lighter shadow.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Only opaque objects can form shadows; translucent and transparent objects cannot.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The black opaque card makes a darker shadow than the white opaque card.

intelligence.enrichment: A shadow is the dark region on a screen where light does not reach because an object blocks light falling on that screen. When an object blocks light from reaching a surface, the blocked region on that surface becomes a shadow; stronger blocking produces a darker shadow. The learner correctly applies this rule: A shadow is the dark region on a screen where light does not reach because an object blocks light falling on that screen. A shadow is just the dark color of the object copied onto the wall.
